title: CLIP170 enhancing FOSL1 expression via attenuating ubiquitin-mediated degradation of beta-catenin drives renal cell carcinoma progression.
authors: Huang, Yuanbin; Wen, Zhihao; Tao, Shuyao; Yu, Zhenlong; Wang, Xiaogang; Li, Xiancheng; Gao, Lu
journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CLIP170通过抑制beta-catenin泛素化降解上调FOSL1表达促进肾癌进展，虽涉及蛋白互作和分子对接，但核心是蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Protein interactions are fundamental for all cellular metabolic activities. Cytoplasmic linker protein 170 (CLIP170) plays diverse roles in cellular processes and the development of malignant tumors. Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) poses a significant challenge in oncology owing to its invasive nature, metastatic potential, high recurrence rates, and poor prognosis. However, the specific mechanisms and roles of CLIP170 underlying its involvement in RCC progression remain unclear. The findings of this study revealed a significant upregulation of CLIP170 in RCC tumor tissues. Elevated CLIP170 expression correlated positively with advanced clinical and pathological stages and was associated with poor overall survival in RCC patients. Functional assays in vitro demonstrated that elevated CLIP170 levels enhanced RCC cell proliferation, migration and invasion. Mechanistically, 4D-label free proteomics library identified that CLIP170 increased the level of FOSL1 in the Wnt signaling pathway. Immunoprecipitation and molecular docking were performed to unveil that CLIP170 formed a complex with beta-catenin, inhibiting beta-catenin degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. Elevated beta-catenin levels within RCC cells played a central role in promoting the transcriptional expression of FOSL1, thereby facilitating RCC cell proliferation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) progression. In vivo investigations corroborated these findings, illustrating that CLIP170 regulated beta-catenin and FOSL1 expression, driving tumor growth in RCC. This study highlights the crucial role of CLIP170 in promoting FOSL1 expression by preventing beta-catenin ubiquitination and degradation, thus promoting RCC tumor progression. It suggests the CLIP170/beta-catenin/FOSL1 axis as a potential therapeutic target for RCC treatment.
abstract_zh: 蛋白质相互作用是所有细胞代谢活动的基础。细胞质连接蛋白170（CLIP170）在细胞过程和恶性肿瘤发展中发挥多种作用。肾细胞癌（RCC）因其侵袭性、转移潜力、高复发率和不良预后，在肿瘤学中构成重大挑战。然而，CLIP170在RCC进展中涉及的具体机制和作用仍不清楚。本研究结果揭示了CLIP170在RCC肿瘤组织中显著上调。CLIP170表达升高与晚期临床和病理分期正相关，并与RCC患者总生存期较差相关。体外功能实验表明，CLIP170水平升高增强了RCC细胞的增殖、迁移和侵袭能力。机制上，4D无标记蛋白质组学文库鉴定出CLIP170在Wnt信号通路中增加了FOSL1的水平。通过免疫沉淀和分子对接实验揭示，CLIP170与β-catenin形成复合物，通过泛素-蛋白酶体途径抑制β-catenin降解。RCC细胞内升高的β-catenin水平在促进FOSL1转录表达中发挥核心作用，从而促进RCC细胞增殖和上皮-间质转化（EMT）进程。体内研究证实了这些发现，表明CLIP170调控β-catenin和FOSL1表达，驱动RCC肿瘤生长。本研究强调了CLIP170通过阻止β-catenin泛素化和降解来促进FOSL1表达的关键作用，从而促进RCC肿瘤进展，并提示CLIP170/β-catenin/FOSL1轴可作为RCC治疗的潜在靶点。
